column3: Close to the Greek; “to be greatly awe-struck” is rendered “to be troubled.”
NKJV has “when He returned, He found them asleep again,” following the Textus Receptus word order; the critical text reads “again having come, He found them sleeping.”
Close to the Greek; NKJV renders the statement “Are you sleeping …” as a question, which the Greek allows.
NKJV has “a great multitude,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “a crowd.”
NKJV repeats “Rabbi, Rabbi!,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “Rabbi” once.
Close to the Greek; NKJV supplies “must” in “the Scriptures must be fulfilled.”
Close to the Greek; “officers” is rendered “servants.”
